title: 第69章 饭桌叙旧，白月光的回眸
content_zh:
第69章 饭桌叙旧，白月光的回眸-《重生2000：撕了协议我暴富了》

老弄堂私房菜。

林川推门进去的时候，夏若冰已经坐在靠窗那张桌子了。

头发散着，穿了件米白色的薄毛衣，袖子拢到手腕。

面前一杯柠檬水，杯壁上凝了层水珠，到了有一会儿了。

林川拉开椅子坐下。

两个人对上视线。

隔了两秒，她先开口。

“你瘦了。”

“高中那会儿一百四，现在一百五。哪儿瘦了？”

“不是身材。”夏若冰低头搅了一下柠檬水。“是脸。棱角比以前深了。”

“那叫成熟。”

“……随你怎么说。”

服务员过来递菜单。林川翻了两页，指了几个菜名。

红烧肉、葱油拌面、清炒河虾仁、腌笃鲜。

“你还是老样子。”夏若冰撑着下巴看他。“什么场合都点红烧肉。”

“高中食堂要是有红烧肉，我能连吃三碗饭。”

“你就是因为每次叫人家打菜阿姨'大妈'，所以肉永远只给你两片。”

“差不多的意思。”

“差很多。”

两个人都笑了。

笑完之后，气氛松下来大半。

“林川，你现在做什么？”

“投资。”

“张虎跟我说你在上海开了个挺大的公司。”

“还行，饿不死。”

夏若冰抬了一下头。

“你开宾利来的吧。我进门之前看到弄堂口停了一辆。”

林川没否认。

“那还说饿不死。”

“车又不能当饭吃。”

夏若冰摇头，没再追问。

她不傻。那天在徐家汇的法式餐厅，林川坐的位置、穿的衣服、

手腕上那块叫不出名字但一看就不便宜的表——拼在一起，答案已经很清楚了。

但她不想聊钱。至少不是今天。

菜陆续上来。红烧肉的酱香飘过来，两个人的注意力被岔开了。

林川夹了一块肉，嚼了两下，点头。“这家厨子行。”

“说说你这些年。”夏若冰放下筷子。

“怎么从老家跑到上海来的？”

“出来折腾。一开始什么都干，运气比较好，赶上了几个风口。”

“林川，你从高中开始就喜欢说'还行''运气好'这种话。你以为别人听不出来？”

“那你想听什么？”

“真话。”

林川放下筷子。

“真话就是——吃过很多亏，摔过很多跟头，遇过一些不是人的人，”

“有些离奇的经历，之后就是一路往前走，到现在。”

夏若冰没接话。

过了好几秒。

“你不像是会吃亏的人。”

“那是现在。”林川把碗里最后一口面挑起来。

“以前的时候，吃的亏比你想象的多。”

安静了一小段。

“那你呢。”林川抬头。“怎么跑上海来了？”

夏若冰端着杯子，手指在杯沿上转了一圈。

“大学在武汉读的。毕业回老家待了一年，找不到像样的工作。”

Private kitchen in the old alley.

When Lin Chuan pushed the door open and walked in, Xia Ruobing was already sitting at the table by the window.

Her hair was loose and she was wearing a thin off-white sweater with sleeves rolled up to her wrists.

There was a glass of lemonade in front of me. There were water droplets on the wall of the glass for a while.

Lin Chuan pulled out a chair and sat down.

The two people met their eyes.

After two seconds, she spoke first.

"You've lost weight."

"One hundred and four in high school, one hundred and five now. Where have you lost weight?"

"It's not the figure." Xia Ruobing lowered her head and stirred the lemonade."It's the face. The edges and corners are deeper than before."

"That's called maturity."

"...whatever you say."

The waiter came and handed the menu.Lin Chuan flipped through two pages and pointed out the names of several dishes.

Braised pork, noodles with scallion oil, stir-fried river shrimps, pickled fish.

"You're still the same." Xia Ruobing looked at him with her chin propped up.“Order the braised pork for any occasion.”

"If the high school cafeteria had braised pork, I could eat three bowls of rice in a row."

"It's because you call the vegetable auntie 'Auntie' every time, so I only give you two slices of meat."

"That's pretty much it."

"It's much different."

Both men laughed.

After laughing, the atmosphere relaxed for the most part.

"Linchuan, what are you doing now?"

"Investment."

"Zhang Hu told me that you opened a very big company in Shanghai."

"It's okay, I won't starve to death."

Xia Ruobing raised her head.

"You came in a Bentley. I saw one parked at the entrance of the alley before I entered."

Lin Chuan did not deny it.

"That means I won't starve to death."

"A car can't be used as food."

Xia Ruobing shook her head and didn't ask any more questions.

She's not stupid.That day at the French restaurant in Xujiahui, where Lin Chuan sat, what he wore,

The unnamed watch on my wrist, but it doesn't look cheap at first glance - when put together, the answer is already very clear.

But she didn't want to talk about money.At least not today.

The dishes are coming one after another.The aroma of braised pork wafted over, and the two people's attention was diverted.

Lin Chuan picked up a piece of meat, chewed it twice, and nodded."This chef's shop."

"Tell me about these years." Xia Ruobing put down her chopsticks.

"How did you come to Shanghai from your hometown?"

"Come out and work hard. I did everything at the beginning. I was lucky and caught a few opportunities."

"Linchuan, you've been fond of saying things like 'it's okay' and 'good luck' since high school. Do you think others can't hear it?"

"Then what do you want to hear?"

"The truth."

Lin Chuan put down his chopsticks.

"The truth is - I have suffered a lot, fallen a lot, and met some people who are not human beings,"

"There were some bizarre experiences, and then it just kept moving forward until now."

Xia Ruobing didn't answer.

Several seconds passed.

"You don't seem like someone who's going to suffer."

"That's now." Lin Chuan picked up the last bite of noodles in the bowl.

"In the past, you suffered more losses than you imagined."

It was quiet for a while.

"What about you?" Lin Chuan raised his head."Why did you come to Shanghai?"

Xia Ruobing held the cup and turned her fingers around the rim.

"I studied in college in Wuhan. After graduation, I went back to my hometown for a year and couldn't find a decent job."
